author_note: Checked by hand against the Spanish source. Russian is the easy case for these models — most have seen far more of it than of Bulgarian — so a failure here is a strong signal.

checks.label: te amo -> я тебя люблю
checks.why: First person to second. A model that writes 'ты меня любишь' has swapped who loves whom

checks.label: cómo estás -> как ты
checks.why: A direct question to the mother

checks.label: espero que tengas -> надеюсь
checks.why: A wish, not an assertion that she is having one

checks.label: que sepas -> she should know
checks.why: 'que sepas' asks her to know something. 'Знай, что' is the idiomatic form and 'Пусть ты знаешь' is awkward, but both carry the meaning — style is not what this scores

checks.label: te extraño -> скучаю
checks.why: Unlike Bulgarian, 'скучаю по тебе' is the correct Russian idiom

checks.label: disfrutes este día
checks.why: A wish that she enjoy the day. Russian has many natural renderings — 'пусть тебе понравится', 'пусть будет приятным', 'наслаждайся' — and all of them count

penalties.label: Bulgarian or Ukrainian bleed
penalties.why: The mirror of the Bulgarian failure — a model answering in the wrong Slavic language

penalties.label: untranslated Spanish left in
penalties.why: Source words surviving into the translation
